Warlock · Meta

Apocalypse Warlock

stack-and-detonate ultimate caster

Warlock meta unchanged stack-and-detonate ultimate caster

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 14

Move on whenLevel 70 with Torment 1 unlocked, which is where the endgame guide begins and where the gear chase starts in earnest.
Move on whenHands of the Worldbreaker and Fleshwrit Carapace both equipped, with the Rite of the Nameless charm set coming online - at which point Sigil of Chaos automates itself and comes off the bar.
Move on whenThe full endgame kit - five-piece Rite of the Nameless, 40% crit, the Mythics - and Pit 120 or above as your target content.

Skill bar

1Doom
2Umbral Chains
3Command Valloch
4Sigil of Chaos
5Nether Step
6Apocalypse

Rotation

After the level-32 respec: open with Command Valloch for resources and Overpower, then spam Umbral Chains to load Apocalypse stacks and fire Annihilation at max stacks. Sigil of Chaos on cooldown, Nether Step on cooldown for travel and to break crowd control, and Doom only when Wrath runs dry - resources are not a real problem here thanks to Command Valloch and Wrath Refund.

Skill point priority

  1. The one real weakness of this levelling route, in the guide's own words: 'you have to wait until level 32 to play it'. Until then you run a Lunatic shell - Command Fallen as generator and main damage, Bombardment from level 3 as the AoE spam, base Nether Step at 4, Rampage at 8 fed by Dominance, Summon Ae'grom from the Legion Shard at 15, and Terror Swarm at 22 until Metamorphosis at 25
  2. At level 32, respec. Umbral Chains unlocks Chain Whips and you take Annihilation, which 'allows you to use the ultimate with no cooldown after ramping up Annihilation stacks with Hellfire skills'
  3. How many Umbral Chains casts you need scales with the pack: 'depending on the number of enemies present, you need more or fewer casts to reach 100 stacks (ideally only cast at max.)'
  4. Soul Shard from level 15 is the Ritualist Shard, for Command Valloch's resources and Overpower
  5. Fragment from level 30: run Twisted Fragment while levelling. Scorching Fragment is stronger but costs you Life, so only take it once you can afford the healing
  6. After 32, 'fill up all skill ranks on your primary abilities with leftovers spent on utility skills' - 83 points in total including 14 from Season Rank

Skill bar

1Doom
2Umbral Chains
3Command Valloch
4Sigil of Chaos
5Nether Step
6Apocalypse

Rotation

Command Valloch at the start of every run and roughly every 20 seconds after, for resources and Overpower. Spam Umbral Chains to build stacks, then release Annihilation - ideally at maximum stacks rather than early. Sigil of Chaos on cooldown, Doom only to refill resources, Nether Step for mobility and to break crowd control.

Skill point priority

  1. Chase Hands of the Worldbreaker immediately - 'the key item for this build, enabling a big damage boost and Sigil synergies. Go for this right away when you get started'
  2. Cast Sigil of Chaos as often as physically possible for the Hands of the Worldbreaker multiplier; one or two Sigil Duration tempers keep it up permanently
  3. Aspect of Accursed Touch for near-permanent Vulnerable uptime - it is the build's only Vulnerable source
  4. Only swap to Scorching Fragment once healing is solved: imprint Undying Aspect, transfigure it onto the amulet, or take a large Life on Hit weapon roll
  5. Stat priority skews to multipliers for Vulnerable, Fire and All Damage, plus Attack Speed and Willpower. Crit is deliberately deferred: 'crit chance/multi later once you have acquired the full Rite of the Nameless set and Aspect of Calamity'

Skill bar

1Bombardment
2Umbral Chains
3Command Valloch
4Dark Prison
5Rampage
6Apocalypse

Rotation

Command Valloch on the pull and every 20 seconds after. Spam Umbral Chains to build stacks for Annihilation. Cast Bombardment on Endless Barrage 'once every 10sec to passively apply the Anathema of the Primes buff to enemies around you', and jump pack to pack with Rampage on Demonic Smash - on elites and bosses, hit them once with it for the same buff. Dark Prison whenever it is ready, for Weaken, Fortify and damage reduction.

Skill point priority

  1. Fleshwrit Carapace changes the build rather than improving it: it 'automatically activates your Sigils whenever they are created', and it gives Apocalypse the Sigil tag so the Ultimate itself feeds Rite of the Nameless. At the five-piece, Sigil of Chaos leaves the bar entirely
  2. Anathema of the Primes is what buys the new bar - it 'allows you to replace Nether Step with Rampage - Demonic Smash to move around much faster'. Note it is a Talisman charm, not a weapon
  3. Moloch's Beating Flame is the other major multiplier, worth up to five Hellfire skills buffed by Volatility
  4. Crit comes online now: multipliers for Vulnerable, Crit, Fire and All Damage, plus Attack Speed and Willpower, targeting 40% crit chance with the rest supplied by Aspect of Calamity
  5. If you run dry on resources, 'add extra Wrath Regeneration or Resource Generation to Helm, Boots and Rings'
  6. Transfiguration becomes a real damage layer: '[x] Elemental Multiplier (Fire) is the best outcome in every slot as they are individual multipliers with high values'

Skill bar

1Bombardment
2Umbral Chains
3Command Valloch
4Dark Prison
5Rampage
6Apocalypse

Rotation

The same loop as the late endgame, played with more discipline about uptime. Keep Anathema of the Primes applied by casting Bombardment roughly every 10 seconds and tagging every elite and boss once with Rampage; hold Command Valloch to its 20-second cadence for Overpower; and hold Annihilation for full stacks rather than dumping it early, because on a push floor the pack will still be alive when you get there.

Skill point priority

  1. The guide is explicit that this is not a different build: 'this setup is largely the same as the Endgame variant, optimized for high tier pushing (120+). The main difference is the paragon board'
  2. The paragon swap is the change: 'this setup drops Pyrosis for Fathomless to get a more powerful consistent damage buff as monsters generally live much longer in a push'
  3. The Grandfather earns its slot here mainly as a crit enabler rather than as raw damage
  4. Ring of Starless Skies matters more here, because Rampage jumping burns resources
  5. Toughness checklist: greater-affix Life rolls masterworked on weapons, the defensive runes Que and Lac, 'pick defensive Paragon nodes before offensive/scaling glyph effects', and swap jewellery gems to the threat you are facing - 'generally Fire, Lightning and Poison are the most dangerous'

Board & glyph focus

Glyph level order, identical here and at every later stage: Wrath, Unbound, Empowered, Hellforge, Occultist. Gambling guidance while levelling, by slot: offensive aspects onto gloves, defensive onto chest and pants, utility and mobility onto boots, resource onto rings. Best levelling runewords are Cir with Ceh, which spawns wolves that damage and freeze, and Cem with Qua for a free movement-speed buff on every evade.

Board & glyph focus

Glyph order: Wrath, Unbound, Empowered, Hellforge, Occultist. Board strategy while your paragon level is still low is the guide's Board Rush: 'if you are low Paragon (<200), use the Board Rush step to grab all the important multipliers early and respec later'. The Ritualist Shard is the class-mechanic pick at every stage - almost every skill in the build is an Occult skill, and the Overpower synergies exist specifically to get more out of it.

Same glyph order. Farm paragon deliberately - the FAQ asks for at least 250 and 'ideally closer to 280 to get most of the useful nodes on all boards'. How to run them

The guide switches the hire once, at the levelling-to-endgame line. While levelling it hires Varyana 'for more healing and Vulnerable uptime', taking Taste of Flesh for the healing and Hysteria for attack speed. From the Starter variant onward - and identically across Starter, Midgame, Endgame and Tower Push - it hires Raheir 'for more survivability and Inspiration', which is the tree recorded above. The Reinforcement never changes at any stage: Aldkin, 'for damage reduction from Field of Languish'. Read the whole slot as damage control rather than damage: it is spent entirely on the cons box's 'mediocre survivability' and on the Scorching Fragment self-burn.

Plan

Said plainly: this guide publishes a War Plans section containing six embedded widgets and not one word of prose - no node names, no priorities, no explanation. The picks below are decoded from the guide's own planner payload, where the allocation is byte-identical across all six profiles from levelling through Tower Push, so there is no stage-by-stage progression to describe either. That makes these the author's real board but leaves them unexplained; the notes here say what each node is for from the general War Plans reference, and nothing has been invented about why this build in particular wants them.

Allocation picks9 picks

  • 01Writhe and Rot

    Helltide. Hellwyrm experience and Lair Keys - and this build needs four separate boss-farmed uniques.

  • 02Hellmouth

    Helltide. Opens the Hellwyrm route.

  • 03Grigoire's Gambit

    Lair Bosses. Grigoire is the source of Hands of the Worldbreaker, the build's stated first chase item.

  • 04Two by Two

    Lair Bosses. Two Initiate bosses per Nemesis Lair, which halves the key cost of that chase.

  • 05Jade Epiphany

    Kurast Undercity. Attunement into experience orbs at +1 Monster Power - and this build wants paragon badly, its own FAQ asking for 250 minimum and 'ideally closer to 280'.

  • 06Gutter Filth

    Kurast Undercity.

  • 07Tree of Plenty

    Tree of Whispers.

  • 08Heart of Stone

    The Pit.

  • 09Choron's Blessing

    The Pit. Extra glyph-upgrade chances across Wrath, Unbound, Empowered, Hellforge and Occultist.

Uniques & where to find them

Hands of the Worldbreakergloves

Target-farm Grigoire, The Galvanic Saint. Mythic priority #1 and the guide's instruction is unambiguous: 'the key item for this build, enabling a big damage boost and Sigil synergies. Go for this right away when you get started.'

Where →
Fleshwrit Carapacechest

Target-farm Lord Zir. Mythic priority #2, and the item that changes the build's shape rather than just its numbers: it auto-activates your Sigils and gives Apocalypse the Sigil tag, which is what lets the Ultimate feed the Rite of the Nameless set.

Where →
Moloch's Beating Flameamulet

Target-farm The Butcher. Mythic priority #3, described as 'a major damage boost as we have up to 5 Hellfire skills buffed by Volatility'.

Where →
Ring of Starless Skiesring 1

Mythic Unique, priority #4. Any lair boss can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time. It matters most once you are jumping between packs with Rampage; before you have it, add one or two Resource Generation rolls to your gear.

Where →
The Grandfatherweapon

Mythic Unique, priority #5 and the last thing you should chase. All lair bosses can drop it, or craft it in the Horadric Cube. The guide is measured about it: it 'only slightly beats Cremator's Aspect, but it makes reaching 40% crit a lot easier', which is its real job here.

Where →

Loot filter

maxroll.gg
Apocalypse Warlock — Maxroll Soft / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes)

The guide ships three filters as import codes in its Loot Filter section, added 2026-06-30 per its own changelog. That is the exact match. No Apocalypse-Warlock filter could be verified on the community sites - diablofilter.com's browse page does support filtering by Warlock but no individual filter page was confirmed, so no permalink is offered rather than one being guessed at.

Summary

The Warlock's best pushing build, on the class every fresh source ranks last. The damage is a single screen-wide Annihilation detonation: 'this build uses Umbral Chains - Chain Whips to quickly build Apocalypse stacks to unleash a massive Annihilation explosion every few seconds, evaporating entire screens at once'. Annihilation normally carries a long Ultimate cooldown, and Chain Whips feeds stacks fast enough to circumvent it, so the Ultimate becomes a rhythm rather than a cooldown. Three scaling layers stack on top: Fire and Hellfire multipliers, an Overpower package built from the Ritualist Shard, Command Valloch and Tidal Aspect, and at the top end the Rite of the Nameless charm set, which pays out for casting Sigil skills - and once Fleshwrit Carapace gives Apocalypse the Sigil tag, the Ultimate feeds that set itself. Standing, stated without inflation: Maxroll's overall endgame list rates this B; Maxroll's push list rates it A, where Apocalypse and Lunatic are the two best Warlock entries. TierListHQ rates the class B and last, summarising the season as the largest buff pass and still last, 'fun does not equal meta'. Icy Veins lists three S-tier Warlock builds but that list predates 3.1.1 and is the season's widest source disagreement, so nothing here rests on it. Maxroll's own cons box is the honest expectation: combo build, damage ramping, mediocre survivability. The survivability problem is partly self-inflicted and you should plan for it before you gear - Scorching Fragment burns you when you attack, which is why the guide opens its equipment section insisting you carry healing via Undying Aspect, a transfigured copy on the amulet, or a large Life on Hit weapon roll. One staleness note the guide does not make itself: it was last updated 2026-06-30, on patch 3.1.0, and has not been revised for 3.1.1 or 3.1.2.
